Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the performance characteristics and the cost transparency. Procurement asked me to get a simple annual commit overview (Starter / Growth / Enterprise token tiers) so they can scope a PO and check budget. Can you send a concise proposal that includes:

- Tiered commit sizes (tokens/month and annualized)
- Per-token list price and committed discount % by tier
- Any minimum spend or ramp expectations
- Payment terms and invoicing cadence (Net 30 vs Net 45)

I've attached the SOW draft our legal team started (FinTechCo_SOW_draft.pdf). We're targeting a January 1 start date if we can align pricing + PO by mid-December.

Appreciate keeping the options simple — procurement will route the best-fit tier up to our CFO.

Best,
Laura
Laura Mitchell
Head of AI Partnerships | FinTechCo
Attachments: FinTechCo_SOW_draft.pdf
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Laura Mitchell <laura.mitchell@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Annual commit options and pricing — FinTechCo

Laura — thanks, and great to hear the demo landed. Attached is a short pricing matrix (redwood_commit_pricing_table.xlsx) with three straightforward annual commit paths. High-level summary below; I can hop on a quick 20-min call if you want to walk through numbers.

Proposal (annual committed token bundles):
- Starter: 5M tokens/month (60M tokens/yr) — committed discount: 12% off list (per-token pricing: $0.0009)
- Growth: 25M tokens/month (300M tokens/yr) — committed discount: 22% off list (per-token pricing: $0.0007)
- Enterprise: 100M tokens/month (1.2B tokens/yr) — committed discount: 32% off list (per-token pricing: $0.0005)

Notes:
- Price is for hosted API usage; embeddings and reranking count at same token model but we can carve out exceptions if needed.
- Standard payment: Net 30. We can do Net 45 for Enterprise with a 1.5% surcharge or reclaim via higher commit offset.
- Minimum billing: monthly invoicing against committed monthly spend; overage billed at list price less an agreed overage discount if you exceed committed amounts.

I've CC'd Marissa and Aditya — Marissa is our AE for approvals and any concession requests, Aditya handles finance approvals for non-standard payment terms.

Attachments: redwood_commit_pricing_table.xlsx

Next steps: if Starter/Growth/Enterprise feels right, tell me which tier procurement prefers and any payment constraints. I'll draft a short amendment to the SOW and a DocuSign-ready schedule.

Thanks,
Dylan
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:35:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: FinTechCo pricing ask — recommended concessions

Marissa / Aditya — quick internal note (replying in-thread so Laura has context but this is internal guidance).

Context: FinTechCo is evaluating three tiers. Procurement tends to push for Net 45 and wants a PO/DocuSign fast (target mid-Dec). They're price sensitive but value predictable spend.

My read: we should hold list for Starter, give small flexibility on Growth (up to 24% discount max if they commit to 18-month ramp), and consider a one-time onboarding credit for Enterprise rather than deeper per-token cuts.

Suggested internal approvals:
- Approve Net 45 for Growth with a 1% surcharge recoverable over first 3 invoices (finance signoff needed).
- Approve up to an additional 2% discount at Enterprise only if they sign a 24-month contract and prepay 6 months.
- Approve a $15k onboarding credit for technical integration (one-time).

Aditya — can you confirm finance OKs Net 45 with surcharge and the mechanics for applying onboarding credit? Marissa — please advise if we should push any usage-metering clauses into the SOW (prefix caching/KV cache retention SLA notes).

I'll hold off sending anything that requires leadership signoff until I hear back.

Thanks,
Dylan
From: Laura Mitchell <laura.mitchell@fintechco.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: FinTechCo Procurement <procurement@fintechco.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Annual commit options and pricing — FinTechCo

Dylan — thanks for the quick turnaround and the matrix. A few procurement clarifying points before we escalate to CFO: 

1) Payment: CFO prefers Net 45 but can consider Net 30 if there is a small early-pay discount. Net 45 is our default for SaaS vendors.
2) Ramp: we'd likely start at 50% of the Growth tier for Q1 and step up to full commit by Q3 — is that acceptable operationally (prorated monthly billing)?
3) Contract term: prefer 12 months to start, open to 24 if pricing materially improves.
4) PO path: procurement needs a DocuSign-ready SOW and an invoice/line-item breakdown to generate the PO.

Can you send a version of the SOW with the selected tier and the fee schedule (monthly amounts) so procurement can fast-track? We'd like to circulate to internal stakeholders today.

Also, please include any standard security and data handling hooks in the SOW (SOC2 attestation link is sufficient).

Best,
Laura
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Laura Mitchell <laura.mitchell@fintechco.com>, FinTechCo Procurement <procurement@fintechco.com>

Final pricing summary (annualized):
- Growth (committed): 25M tokens/month (300M tokens/yr) — base per-token: $0.0007 (22% off list)
- Q1 staged start: billing at 50% of the monthly committed rate, with true-up and token reconciliation at the end of Q2
- Payment terms: Net 45 (approved) — Redwood applies a 1.0% administrative surcharge to offset extended terms; discount profile preserved
- One-time onboarding credit: $15,000 applied on invoice #2 after go-live

Action items attached: SOW amendment pre-filled (FinTechCo_SOW_draft.pdf - updated), fee schedule spreadsheet (redwood_commit_pricing_table.xlsx), and DocuSign link to sign: https://www.docusign.net/Signing/?t=example-doc-id

HubSpot: I've created the deal record (https://app.hubspot.com/deal/23456) and populated the negotiated terms.

If procurement is comfortable, please sign the DocuSign schedule and route a PO to billing@redwood.com. We'll assign a Solutions Engineer to start integration planning immediately after signature.

Thanks everyone — happy to jump on a 15-min call if you want to review the ramp mechanics.

Best,
